runtime_uncertainties: This law selects near-side crosswalk before stop line; do not import the different NRS 484B.257(1) hierarchy.
Native trigger does not establish proper official sign erection or sidewalk-derived crosswalk boundary.
A sampled zero-speed frame is physical observation, not an invented statutory duration.
Runner, cameras, finalizer, fallbacks and full proofs remain worker-owned CPU work.
planning_status: partial; Native stop-sign selector and original-frame body halt/crosswalk ordering CPU-tested

requirement_dispositions.requirement: If there is no near-side crosswalk, stop at a clearly marked stop line before entering the intersection
requirement_dispositions.evidence_or_gap: Original marked line, complete body and stop history measured; marking authority and legal qualification unresolved

requirement_dispositions.requirement: If there is neither crosswalk nor marked stop line, stop at the nearest point with a view of approaching intersecting-highway traffic
requirement_dispositions.evidence_or_gap: Sampled first-view proxy needs original actor and ray packets; legal nearest point and driver view unresolved

requirement_dispositions.requirement: Every driver approaching a stop intersection indicated by a stop sign shall stop before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection
requirement_dispositions.evidence_or_gap: Marked or opposed-sidewalk-derived near-side geometry and complete-body halt are measured; proper sign and legal crosswalk status unresolved

dev.stop_sign.evidence: Native governing stop sign identified from the approach waypoint; sign identity retained in original approach context.

dev.governs.evidence: Native sign trigger and approach road/lane identity are checked before capture; governance remains subject to physical review.

st.lane_enters.evidence: Native approach waypoint road/lane ID is matched to the sourced site and retained through reference entry.

drv.approaching.evidence: Original ego transform, road/lane and frame history show approach progression toward the selected intersection.

st.crosswalk.evidence: Native map crosswalk is checked against the site polygon; marked and unmarked dispositions are recorded in case-specific approach context.

st.stop_line.evidence: When present, sourced site marked-line segment and original ego body positions locate the selected stop reference; absence is explicit in other branches.

st.intersection.evidence: Sourced intersection polygon and original body vertices locate entry and complete clearance; Native waypoint checks the approach lane.

st.sight_distance.evidence: In the no-crosswalk/no-line case, original sampled traffic visibility and observer context identify first observed view; nearest legal point remains unresolved.

rel.visible.evidence: Original visible-traffic IDs are joined to each sight sample; this is a sampled proxy, with actual driver sight and occlusion awaiting Native review.

drv.stopped.evidence: Original speed and complete body vertices identify a zero-speed halt and its frame before the selected reference.

drv.crossing_line.evidence: Original complete-body footprint is compared with crosswalk or marked-line geometry at synchronized frames.

drv.entering_intersection.evidence: Original complete-body footprint is joined to the sourced intersection polygon and Native frame map.
